concepts.def: How thick or runny a liquid is
Temperature at which a liquid becomes a gas
How easily a substance catches fire and burns
Shows how atoms are joined by lines for bonds
All carbon–carbon bonds are single bonds
Orange bromine water decolourises with alkenes

walkthroughs.body_html:
As chain length goes up, properties change in a pattern.

Longer chains: boiling point ↑, viscosity ↑ (thicker), flammability ↓ (harder to ignite).

Short chains (methane, propane) are gases that ignite easily. Long chains (bitumen) are thick, sticky and hard to burn.

Each line is a bond. Carbon makes 4 bonds, hydrogen makes 1.

Ethane has two carbons joined by a single line, each carbon also joined to 3 H atoms. Ethene has two carbons joined by a double line (C=C), each carbon also joined to 2 H atoms.

Add a few drops of orange bromine water to the sample and shake.

With an alkene: bromine adds across the C=C bond and the orange colour decolourises (goes colourless).

With an alkane: no reaction, orange colour stays.
